newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan housing completions fell 9.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan housing completions fell 9.9 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:
The 9.9 percent drop in January housing completions was the biggest decline since a 6.9 percent decrease in February 1996.
The department said completions of single-family homes fell 7.4 percent in January, the biggest decline since a 7.1 percent drop in February 1996.

The department revised December single-family completions to a 1.4 percent rise and November to a 1.9 percent increase. Previously, it said single-family completions rose 1.1 percent in December and increased 1.4 percent in November.

January multi-family unit completions fell 19.5 percent after a revised 7.9 percent rise in December and a revised 13.8 percent jump in November. Previously, the department said December multi-family unit completions rose 11.4 percent and that November multi-family unit completions were up 13.3 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis fell in January to 91,900 units from 141,100 units in December and from 122,700 units in November. In January 1996, actual completions were reported at 99,300.

Privately-owned housing units under construction rose to a seasonally adjusted 822,000 in January from 817,000 in December but fell from 828,000 in November. They compare with 802,000 units under construction in January 1996.
